subject: Argentum on-prem throttle pattern — production latency & throughput impact
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@argentum.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@argentum.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — urgent

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency and a drop in sustained throughput on our on-prem deployment around 08:45 PDT this morning. User-facing queries are timing out (503) and token generation appears to be doubling for identical prompts. Attached is a sample request_id_20260721.log plus a short timeline from our side.

What we observed: 
- p95 latency jumped from ~420ms to ~2.4s between 08:45–09:00
- overall requests/sec dropped ~35% while retry counts increased
- KV cache eviction events spiked in the attached snippet

This is affecting a small set of enterprise customers; can you triage? Happy to provide any more traces.

Thanks,
Sara Lim
SRE Lead, Argentum Systems

Attachments: request_id_20260721.log
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@argentum.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, DevOps Team <devops@argentum.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — urgent

Hi Sara — thanks for the quick heads up and the log. We’re starting a triage now. Two quick asks that will speed diagnosis: 

1) Can you share the last 30 minutes of node-level GPU metrics and the scheduler logs (container restarts / OOM / eviction events)?
2) If you have a short sample request payload (anonymized) and the model version pinned for the affected route, please attach.

Immediate actions from our side: Rishi is taking lead on runtime traces, Vivek will look at KV cache behavior and eviction thresholds, and I’ll coordinate with Product for a mitigation path. If we see this is service-impacting for broader customers we’ll engage Execs and propose immediate compensation per SLA.

I’ll update within the hour.

—Kimberly Park
Customer Success (Enterprise) — Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: (none)
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production latency spike — initial triage notes

Forwarding Sara’s report with initial findings from my run:

Summary of quick analysis (observed in their log + traces):
- We are seeing KV cache churn that aligns with a recent rolling restart of their inference cluster at ~08:40. Cache TTLs are short in their config (60s) which exacerbates cold starts for long-context sessions.
- Batching window dropped unexpectedly due to a tight autoscaler threshold; effective batch sizes went from 16 -> 5 at the same time as the p95 jump.
- No obvious OOMs, but there are frequent small restarts of a single worker node (node-07).

Immediate hypothesis: simultaneous rolling restart + aggressive autoscaler + short KV TTLs produced a cascade that increased per-request decoding time and reduced throughput.

Next steps I recommend (low risk, fast):
- Temporarily relax autoscaler lower threshold to avoid under-batching.
- Increase KV cache TTL to 300s for the affected pool.
- If node-07 continues to restart, isolate and repro with debug logging.

I’ll prepare a short runnable checklist for Ops and a short message we can send to the customer.

Attachments: kv-eviction-sample.txt, p95-dash.png
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@argentum.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@argentum.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — mitigation & next steps

Sara — thanks for the patience. We completed the initial triage and executed a short mitigation pack that should reduce user impact while we continue deeper investigation. Summary below: 

What we changed (applied at 11:55 PDT):
- Increased KV cache TTL from 60s -> 300s for the affected model pool.
- Relaxed autoscaler lower bound to prevent batch window collapse (min pods bumped + hold window extended 2m).
- Put a safety fallback: route 5% of traffic to the 1/2-size model variant (faster decode) for the next 60 minutes to reduce tail latency while we verify stability.

Observed immediate effects: 
- p95 decreased from ~2.4s -> ~600ms in the first 20 minutes
- requests/sec creeping back toward expected baseline

Planned follow-ups (today):
- Vivek will investigate node-07 restart cause and verify kernel/drivers.
- Rishi will run a controlled rolling restart with enhanced debug to confirm no regression in batch sizing.
- We’ll prepare a short RCA draft and timeline for your execs by EOD.

We’ve opened internal ticket SUP-8721 and dropped the logs into the shared Drive link. If you’re comfortable, we’d like to request a 60-minute maintenance window tonight at 22:00 PDT to run a controlled repro and a full node hardware check.

If this is insufficient for your customers, we’re prepared to escalate to leadership and discuss credits. Would you like us on an exec call?

—Kimberly

Attachments: argentum_manifest.json
From: John Hayes <john.hayes@argentum.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@argentum.ai>, laura.bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — mitigation & next steps

Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick mitigation. This incident impacted SLA-bound customers and we had visible customer complaints this morning. I appreciate the reduction in p95 but we need a succinct timeline, root cause, and permanent remediation plan.

Requesting: 
- 1-page exec timeline (what happened, impact window, customer impact)
- Proposed permanent fixes and expected timeline for delivery
- Recommendation on credits (we are looking at a 72-hour credit for affected customers unless a different offer is proposed).

We’d like an exec call today at 10:30 PDT for a briefing. Please include Rishi and whoever owns the runtime.

Regards,
John Hayes
CTO, Argentum Systems
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Exec brief draft and call prep (10:30 PDT)

Team — building a 1-pager and short deck for the 10:30 with Argentum. Draft bullets below (will share deck link in 15m):

- Incident summary: rolling restart + aggressive autoscaler + short KV TTL -> cascade causing p95 surge and throughput regression (impact window 08:45–11:55 PDT).
- Immediate mitigations applied (KV TTL, autoscaler hold, 5% fallback to smaller model) and observed improvement.
- Short-term next steps (isolate node-07, controlled rolling restart under debug, extend cache defaults for affected pools).
- Long-term fixes (autoscaler heuristics to avoid under-batching, sticky KV cache on rolling restarts, improved node health detection + replacement).
- Customer ask: propose 48–72 hour credit range; recommend 48h offer with option to escalate depending on final impact audit.

Kimberly — can you confirm the EOD RCA timeline and who will present each bullet? Rishi, please bring the log excerpts and timing. Vivek — please add a short note about kernel/driver checks if node hardware shows anomalies.

—Marcus
